messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - gpu-infer-us-west2: cuda_alloc_failed (OOM) firing for pool infer-us-west2a
pagerduty: Triggered: PD-78521 -> Assigned to oncall (olivia)
olivia: acked PD-78521 :thumbsup: looking into it now, jumping onto node gpunode-17
olivia: quick status: several gpus showing CUDA OOM in nvml logs, model=llama-70b-8bit, seq=2048, sudden mem spike
kevin: which customers affected? any 5xx spikes in frontends?
olivia: frontend metrics show a small bump in 503s for hosted-api-us-west2 (~2.4% over baseline). Affected routes: /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Tagging customers with high qps.
marco: can you paste the nvml snippet?
olivia: ```
Dec 01 12:12:03 gpunode-17 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0: out of memory
Dec 01 12:12:03 inferd[4132]: cuda: cuMemAlloc failed, error=700 (out of memory)
Dec 01 12:12:04 inferd[4132]: model_load: KV cache growth + sudden spike
```
olivia: looks like an unusually large KV cache from a few long-context requests + batching coalesced them
sam: are these batched requests from a single customer or many small ones?
olivia: preliminary trace: 3 large requests (context ~120k tokens) from customer: infra-ml-prod-1 within 30s, they triggered large prefix cache and filled slab allocator
kevin: ok we should mitigate fast: can we evict KV cache or throttle those requests?
marco: I can push a temporary routing rule to throttle max_seq for hosted tier to 8k for 10m, fallback to smaller model. Anyone object?
olivia: do it. Also add a prefix-cache eviction job on that pool (evict keys with owner infra-ml-prod-1)
incident-bot: runbook action: evict_kv_cache --pool infer-us-west2a --owner infra-ml-prod-1 -> queued (job 4592)
pagerduty: PD-78521 acknowledged by olivia at 12:13:05 UTC
kevin: @marco please coordinate with control-plane, need a rollback plan if routing rule causes client regressions
marco: will monitor live traces, I have a safe rollback command: revert-route-rule infer-us-west2a tmp-throttle
olivia: evict job completed, memory freed on GPU0 and GPU1, seeing gradual drop in mem pressure
sam: can we throttle that customer from infra control plane? they have bursty streaming jobs
kevin: paging customer success to inform infra-ml-prod-1. @sre-rotation can you draft a quick note?
sam: drafting: "we observed very large context requests causing GPU mem pressure; we applied temporary throttles and evictions to stabilize. We'll follow up with config suggestions."
olivia: monitoring: host-level metrics back to normal, 503s trending back to baseline. No new OOMs in last 90s
marco: I'm enabling fallback model for any new high-seq requests: llama-70b-8bit -> llama-13b-8bit for hosts on that pool for 15m
pagerduty: PD-78521: Event status -> Resolved (manual) by olivia at 12:15:20 UTC
kevin: good job. Next actions: 1) reach out to infra-ml-prod-1 (CS) 2) add rate-limit and max-context protections to pool config 3) write short incident note in #postmortems if repro steps exist
olivia: capturing notes, will create postmortem stub and assign to marco for change to pool config. Also will add eval to detect sudden kv cache growth in runtime alerts
sam: adding customer contact to thread and pinging support to prep message
marco: one more thing — we saw batching coalescing threshold at 1s causing the 3 requests to batch. Suggest lowering batching window for large-context models in this pool
olivia: agreed. adding to runbook: if KV cache > 60% and incoming seq > 32k -> auto-throttle.
kevin: handoff: I'll be on rotation for next 30m, @olivia keep me posted if it re-fires. Otherwise close PD and add postmortem link once done
olivia: thanks, closing PD now. :white_check_mark:
